title: Implement PostgreSQL backend adapter
description: Add a new backend implementation that talks to PostgreSQL.
design:
Implement PostgreSQL backend using a Postgres driver.

Decide driver:
- Python: psycopg (v3) preferred
- Node: pg
- Go: pgx

Implement CRUD functions and transaction semantics matching SQLite backend.

Pay attention to:
- Parameter placeholders ($1..)
- RETURNING vs last_insert_rowid()
- UPSERT syntax
- Boolean/date/time types
- Concurrency/locking behavior differences
acceptance_criteria:
- Postgres backend implements the backend interface.
- All core operations work against Postgres in manual smoke test.
- Errors are mapped to user-friendly messages (e.g., connection failure, auth, missing DB).

title: Add tests/CI to validate behavior on Postgres and SQLite
description: Ensure automated coverage for both backends, including CI Postgres service container.
design:
Introduce a set of backend contract tests that run against any backend.

- Run existing tests against SQLite.
- Add a Postgres test matrix using a disposable DB (docker-compose / CI service).
- Ensure tests are hermetic: unique schema or database per run.

Add minimum smoke tests for:
- issue create/list/show/update/close
- dependencies/blocked graph
- stats calculations
acceptance_criteria:
- Test suite runs against SQLite and PostgreSQL.
- CI config includes Postgres and runs these tests.
- No backend-specific skips for core behavior.

title: Implement PostgreSQL database backend
description: Add a PostgreSQL backend option (in addition to SQLite) for the library's persistence layer.
design:
Add a PostgreSQL backend alongside the existing SQLite backend.

Key considerations:
- Abstract DB operations behind a backend interface (connect, migrations/schema init, CRUD primitives used by the library).
- Configuration: support selecting backend via env var / config file / connection string.
- SQL compatibility: adjust queries for Postgres (parameter placeholders, returning clauses, UPSERT syntax, foreign keys, etc.).
- Migrations: either maintain neutral migrations or backend-specific; ensure initial schema can be created in Postgres.
- Connection/pooling: use a robust driver (likely psycopg/psycopg2) with pooling and proper transaction handling.
- Testing: run backend contract tests against both SQLite and Postgres; add CI service container for Postgres.

Out of scope (initial epic): performance tuning, advanced pooling, multi-tenant schemas.
acceptance_criteria:
- A new PostgreSQL backend can be selected via configuration and used to run the library without code changes for callers.
- Schema is created/migrated successfully on a fresh Postgres database.
- Core commands/features work end-to-end using Postgres (create/list/show/update/close/dep/etc.).
- Automated tests cover both SQLite and Postgres backends.
- Documentation updated with setup instructions and configuration examples.

title: Abstract persistence layer behind a DB backend interface
description: Refactor current SQLite-backed persistence into a backend interface used across the library/CLI.
acceptance_criteria:
- A backend interface exists that captures all DB operations used by the library.
- SQLite backend implements the interface without behavior regressions.
- Call sites no longer depend on sqlite-specific APIs directly.

title: Add configuration for selecting SQLite vs PostgreSQL backend
description: Add config/env/CLI support for choosing the DB backend and passing connection parameters.
design:
Define a configuration surface for selecting DB backend and providing connection details.

Options (pick one and document):
- Environment variables (e.g., JCE_DB_BACKEND=sqlite|postgres, JCE_DATABASE_URL=...)
- Config file (TOML/YAML/JSON)
- CLI flags (override)

Should support a single Postgres DSN/URL form.
acceptance_criteria:
- Users can select sqlite vs postgres via config.
- Invalid configs produce clear errors.
- Defaults preserve current SQLite behavior.
notes: Starting work: add configuration for selecting sqlite vs postgres backend and passing connection parameters (DSN).

title: Create Postgres schema/migrations equivalent to SQLite
description: Add DDL/migrations so the same logical schema exists in PostgreSQL.
design:
Implement Postgres schema initialization/migrations.

If project uses raw SQL schema:
- Provide equivalent Postgres DDL.

If using a migration tool:
- Ensure migrations run on Postgres.

Ensure:
- Primary keys / types map correctly
- Foreign keys constraints are enforced
- Indexes added where needed
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh Postgres database can be initialized to the required schema.
- Migrations (if any) run cleanly from empty DB to latest.
- Schema parity with SQLite is validated (tables/columns/constraints).
notes: Starting Postgres schema/migrations work: create Postgres DDL equivalent to existing SQLite schema and ensure init path exists.

title: Document PostgreSQL backend setup and configuration
description: Add documentation for using the new Postgres backend.
design:
Update docs with:
- How to install Postgres driver dependency
- How to configure DATABASE_URL/DSN
- How to initialize schema/migrations
- Common troubleshooting (connection refused, auth, permissions)

Include copy-paste examples.
acceptance_criteria:
- README/docs include Postgres setup instructions.
- Configuration examples for both sqlite and postgres are present.
- Any new env vars/flags are documented.
